assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Caplin Point Laboratories (consolidated, ₹ crore), as of 30-Sep-2026 on Q1FY27 results. Net Profit history is the attributable figure (tools/authoring/CAPLIPOINT.patch.js: Screener 'Profit for EPS'); minorities (mainly the 31% of the Guatemala distributor the group does not own) are carried in the tax line (taxBuild), so the model's profit and EPS are to Caplin Point's shareholders. Caplin reports two segments, Rest of the World (Latin America and Africa, 79% of FY26 revenue) and USA (Caplin Steriles, 21%); the engine runs one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path, the segment build sits in `businessLines` and CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue (CAPLIPOINT.mult.js writes revenueGrowth from it). EBITDA is Screener's operating profit, i.e. before other income (the company's own 'EBITDA' of ₹876 cr in FY26 includes ₹116 cr of other income). Other income = treasury yield on the gross treasury book + government grants and miscellaneous income, no FX gains (built in CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js). Screener files the ₹216.6 cr of Caplin Steriles CCPS held by Eight Roads / F-Prime as borrowings; we leave them there (a claim on Caplin Steriles, not Caplin Point equity). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by segment (businessLines; CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js checks the sum). Rest of the World (Latin America + Africa) +14% in FY27E: Q1FY27 +18% (El Salvador tender spill-over, $7 mn of Central American emergency tenders over two quarters, Chile tenders of $12 mn over 18 months); the Vice-Chairman's AR letter lists ~$24 mn of tender wins in Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua plus Chile's $9.5 mn for FY27 against $18 mn a year earlier; in dollars LatAm grew only 3% in FY26 ($150 mn to $155 mn) and Central America 7%, so roughly 6-7 points of FY27E growth is the rupee (FY26 average ₹88.4/$, Mar-26 close ₹94.65/$; AR FY26 AOC-1). FY28E and FY29E +10%: no further currency gain assumed; Chile and Mexico registrations (29 Mexican approvals, 120+ filings planned) start to contribute, management talks of 18-24 months of 'gestation'. USA (Caplin Steriles, incl. its US front-end) +25% in FY27E: guided 25-30% for FY27 (14-May-2026 call), Q1 +26%, own label targeted at ~₹200 cr vs ~₹100 cr; but the plant is 'booked out till February' and Line 7 starts only in 6-7 months (12-Aug-2026 call), and the 10-observation Form 483 of 21-Aug-2026 adds risk. FY28E and FY29E +20%: new capacity (Line 7, then five lines in the COL-II block from Q1FY28) needs 9-10 months of post-approval supplements per product before it sells into the US, so growth slows from FY26's 28% until FY29.

businessLines._why: Segment revenue, consolidated results and AR FY26 note 26 (disaggregation): USA ₹453.40 cr, Rest of the World ₹1,733.79 cr = revenue from operations ₹2,187.19 cr (sale of products ₹2,083.90 cr, service income ₹87.48 cr, export incentives ₹15.81 cr). The USA segment equals Caplin Steriles' consolidated turnover (₹453.40 cr, AR FY26 AOC-1), so it includes CSL's small non-US regulated-market sales.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener operating margin (before other income): 32.6% FY24, 33.6% FY25, 35.0% FY26, 35.0% in Q1FY27 (ICICI Direct table: 34.8% / 35.0%). Gross margin 59.8% in Q1FY27, guided to stay ~60% (CFO, 12-Aug-2026; the long-standing commitment is 55%). Mix helps: Caplin Steriles' EBITDA margin rose to 30% in FY26 (33% in Q4FY26) from 27.9%, and LatAm's PBT margin rose from 42% to 45% (AR FY26). Costs that hold it back: the oncology plant (Caplin One Labs, PBT −₹19 cr in FY26), the Vizag API unit and Amaris Clinical are not yet breaking even (14-May-2026 call); the Rest of World segment's PBT margin slid from 37.5% in Q1FY26 to ~33% in Q1FY27; Middle East war freight and raw-material inflation. FY27E 35.0% (Q1 level). FY28E 34.8%: the COL-II injectable block and the new Pondicherry OSD/derma plant start (Q1FY28) with staff and overheads ahead of revenue. FY29E 35.2%: utilisation and the US mix. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹28 cr of EBITDA (~3% of FY28E EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex ₹248 cr in FY26 (Screener cash flow; CFO 14-May-2026). Of the ~₹1,000-1,100 cr programme, ₹510 cr remained to be spent over 18-24 months from May-2026 (CFO): COL-II injectable block at Gummidipoondi, the Pondicherry OSD/derma plant, the Thervoy oncology API plant, IV-bag line expansion; Q1FY27 capex ₹55 cr. Not in that figure: the Mexico plant (₹100-125 cr, ICICI Direct Q3FY26 note; construction from mid-2027, AR FY26), Chile warehouses and a quality lab, Amaris expansion to 120 beds. FY27E ₹320 cr, FY28E ₹300 cr (programme tail + Mexico start), FY29E ₹220 cr (Mexico completion + maintenance ~₹100 cr).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹72.8 cr = 8.0% of average gross block (₹859 → ₹965 cr, Screener); Q1FY27 ₹21.6 cr (₹86.5 cr annualised) after the oncology injectable plant and CSL Line 6 were capitalised in April 2026. The engine depreciates capex at once while CWIP (₹234 cr) is held flat, so 8.0%: FY27E ~₹90 cr, FY28E ~₹114 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: FY26 treasury income ₹85.3 cr (interest ₹66.34 cr, realised gains ₹16.81 cr, fair-value gains ₹2.14 cr; AR FY26 note 27) on an average treasury book of ₹1,331 cr (cash, bank deposits and current and non-current investments: ₹1,181.9 cr at Mar-25, ₹1,480.1 cr at Mar-26) = 6.4%. The engine applies the yield to its opening net cash, which deducts the ₹216.6 cr CCPS and ₹4.6 cr of leases and loans that Screener files as borrowings; the yield on that gap is added back in otherIncome (CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js), so in effect 6.4% is earned on the whole gross book. Management is moving 'up the risk chain' into credit and debt funds (12-Aug-2026 call); we assume no change in yield.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built in CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js from AR FY26 note 27: (1) 6.4% on the ₹221 cr gap between the gross treasury book and the engine's net cash (the CCPS and leases are not interest-bearing debt), so the yield applies to the whole ₹1,480 cr book; (2) government grants ₹2.38 cr and miscellaneous income ₹9.25 cr (FY26), held flat. Left out: FX gains (₹18.62 cr in FY26, ₹20.78 cr in FY25), which depend on the rupee's fall against the dollar and the currencies of Caplin's markets; a weaker rupee is already in our FY27E revenue. FY27E total other income ≈ ₹106 cr vs ₹115.5 cr reported in FY26 (₹96.9 cr excluding FX) and ₹126 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 including FX.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹0.87 cr (interest on borrowings ₹0.54 cr, leases ₹0.33 cr; AR FY26 note 31); Q1FY27 ₹0.18 cr. No bank debt (Vice-Chairman, 12-Aug-2026).
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: no minority line). Built in `taxBuild`: tax at 20.5% of PBT (FY26 19.1%, Q1FY27 20.5% 'in line with our target of 20%', CFO 12-Aug-2026; ~21% per the Q3FY26 call) plus minorities. Engine rate = (20.5% x PBT + minorities) / PBT, written from the build by CAPLIPOINT.mult.js. The model's profit and EPS are therefore to Caplin Point's shareholders.

taxBuild._note: Engine tax rate = (tax on PBT + minorities) / PBT. ₹ crore.
taxBuild._why: Minorities: FY24 ₹4 cr, FY25 ₹4.78 cr, FY26 ₹8.49 cr, Q1FY27 ₹2.18 cr (Q1FY26 −₹2.04 cr): mainly the 31% of Nuevos Eticos Neo Ethicals S.A., Guatemala (AR FY26 note 43), plus 0.1% of Argus Salud. Grown in line with the Rest of World business. The Eight Roads / F-Prime CCPS in Caplin Steriles take no share of profit in the accounts (they sit inside equity attributable to owners); their claim is shown separately in the valuation.

assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹8 a share (₹4 interim paid 8-Jun-2026 + ₹4 final approved at the 25-Sep-2026 AGM) = ₹60.8 cr, 9.5% of EPS; FY25 ₹6 (8.5%); FY24 ₹5. Caplin has never bought back shares. Management prefers acquisitions (a Mexican or Chilean distributor, ANDAs) and capex, and offers dividends only if no acquisition comes (Chairman, 12-Aug-2026). We keep 10%, so cash builds; no acquisition is modelled.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity: 6.5% + 1.0 x 6% = 12.5%. Caplin has no debt and ₹1,480 cr of gross treasury, so WACC ≈ cost of equity. Beta 1.0, above Ajanta and Ipca (0.8-0.9): small and politically volatile markets (Central America, Ecuador), currency and receivable risk (128 days), one US sterile site carrying a fresh 10-observation Form 483, and a founder-led board.
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5% nominal in rupees: generic volumes in Latin America and US injectables grow mid-single digit in dollars, plus some rupee depreciation.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~12% (FY29E) to 7% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 33%: below the 35% of FY26-27 because the US mix (30% EBITDA margin) rises and LatAm generic pricing is competitive; above the 30-31% of FY21-23.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: 5% of revenue (FY24-26 average ~10% during the ₹1,000 cr programme; FY21-22 ~3-7%).
dcf._depWhy: 3.5% of revenue (FY26 3.3%, rising as the new plants are capitalised).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Latin America keeps growing in the mid-teens as Chile and Mexico tenders and private-market launches scale and the rupee stays weak; the Form 483 closes without escalation, Line 7 and COL-II start on time and the US grows 25-30% a year; the oncology plant and API unit break even.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The 483 escalates (warning letter or import alert) and the US stalls; Central American tenders lapse after FY27 and dollar growth reverts to the 3% of FY26; receivables stretch further in government markets and new plants run below break-even for longer.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Caplin: the only broker note standing on 30-Sep-2026 that discloses a method (ICICI Securities, 13-Aug-2026) uses P/E, 26x FY28E EPS; ICICI used EV/EBITDA until Feb-2026. P/E is also the house method for thinly covered pharma names. 19x Sep-28E EPS = Caplin's 17.7x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (house forwardMedian, 58 points, reported EPS: the company reports no exceptional items; no trough years, EPS rose every year from ₹32.0 in FY21 to ₹84.4 in FY26) x the pharma sector factor of 1.082 (median of the nine-peer set's trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +8.2% for names outside the set, PLAYBOOK §7c A21; reproduced at 8.19%) = 19.2x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. Bull 23x / bear 13.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (21.2x / 12.6x) x the factor. No growth, returns or own-move adjustment; the post-re-rating window since Apr-2024 (21.8x, 24x with the same-window peer move) is a sensitivity row. The model's EPS is EPS to shareholders (minorities in the tax line). Checked in CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js; written by CAPLIPOINT.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check. Caplin's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 15.5x (Screener); times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor (+7.5%, PLAYBOOK §7c A21) = 16.7x, rounded to 16.5x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) plus the engine's net cash at Sep-2027 (which deducts the ₹216.6 cr Caplin Steriles CCPS at book). Bull 20.5x / bear 13x = 75th / 25th percentile x the factor.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at a 12.5% cost of equity, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash (after the CCPS at book).

cover.headline: A cash-rich Latin American generics franchise with a fast-growing US arm, but at 26.4x FY28E EPS the stock prices in far more than its own history, a fresh USFDA Form 483 and slowing dollar growth allow
cover.lead: Caplin Point sells plain generic medicines in small Central and South American markets through its own subsidiaries, warehouses and sales teams (Rest of World, 79% of FY26 revenue), and sterile injectables in the US through Caplin Steriles (21%). It is debt-free with ₹1,480 cr of cash and investments, a 35% EBITDA margin and EPS that has risen every year (₹32.0 in FY21 to ₹84.4 in FY26). Q1FY27 was good (revenue +19.6%, US +26%). But Latin American sales grew only 3% in dollars in FY26; the US plant is full until early 2027 and an unannounced USFDA inspection (13-21 Aug 2026) ended with 10 observations. We forecast EPS of ₹93.4 / 102.9 / 117.0 for FY27-29E. The only broker that discloses a method (ICICI Securities) uses **P/E**, the house method too: **19x Sep-28E EPS (₹109.9)**, Caplin's 17.7x median forward P/E since Apr-2021 lifted 8.2% for pharma's re-rating, gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,258; DCF ₹1,666. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: 5,000+ registrations, own warehouses and 700+ people across Central America and the Caribbean; ~41% shelf share in independent pharmacies there; 60% gross margin; EPS up every year since FY21; capex of ~₹1,000 cr funded entirely from cash flow, with treasury still rising to ₹1,502 cr "free cash" at Jun-26.

arguments.h: But the core is growing slowly
arguments.p: Latin American sales were $155 mn in FY26 vs $150 mn in FY25 (+3%); Central America +7%. Rupee growth (+9.5% for Rest of World) came from the weaker rupee and a large El Salvador tender. Chile and Mexico are years from scale. Receivables (138 days) and inventory (181 days) keep absorbing cash.

arguments.h: The US is the growth, and the risk
arguments.p: Caplin Steriles grew 28% in FY26 to ₹453 cr with a 30% EBITDA margin; 60 ANDAs approved, 38 launched, own label ~₹100 cr. But it is one site, booked out till February, new lines sell into the US only from FY28-29, and the Aug-2026 inspection produced a 10-observation Form 483. Eight Roads and F-Prime hold CCPS that convert into at least 25.29% of Caplin Steriles, which the reported EPS ignores.

arguments.h: Valuation: well above its own history
arguments.p: At ₹2,716 Caplin trades at 31.0x trailing and 26.4x our FY28E EPS, against a 17.7x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021, and 34.2% above its own five-year median trailing P/E (pharma peers +8.2%). ICICI's 26x FY28E (₹2,840) is the only street target. Even the post-re-rating window since Apr-2024 gives 24x, about ₹2,640: below the price.

catalysts: USFDA: Caplin's reply to the 10-observation Form 483 (inspection 13-21 Aug 2026) and the FDA's classification of the inspection (an OAI classification or warning letter would hit US launches and the new lines).
Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): collection of the Q1 receivables build, Rest of World growth after the El Salvador tender, US growth with the plant full.
Capacity: Line 7 at Caplin Steriles (due within 6-7 months of Aug-2026), COL-II construction (Mar-2027) and the Pondicherry OSD plant (Q1FY28).
Latin America: Mexico launches (29 approvals, 120+ filings planned), Chile tenders ($12 mn over 18 months), a distributor acquisition in Mexico or Chile.
Capital allocation: use of the cash pile (acquisitions, credit funds, a higher payout).

sections.title: What Caplin does: a "stock-and-sale" generics distributor in small Latin American markets, plus a US injectables maker

blocks.p: Caplin Point makes and buys generic medicines in India and China and sells them where big companies do not bother. **Rest of the World (₹1,734 cr, 79% of FY26 revenue)** is mostly Central America and the Caribbean (Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Panama, Costa Rica), now extending to Chile, Mexico and Colombia, plus ~3% from French-speaking Africa. Caplin owns the importing and distribution companies in these countries, keeps about six months of fast-moving stock in its own warehouses next to the customer, and sells 300-odd products (tablets, syrups, injections, ointments) straight to pharmacies, through two or three co-distributors per country (10-12% of sales) and to governments in tenders (18-20% in Central America). About 60% is made in its own plants in Puducherry and Chennai; ~40% is bought from Indian (76%) and Chinese (24%) contract makers. **USA (₹453 cr, 21%)** is Caplin Steriles: a sterile injectables and eye-drops plant at Gummidipoondi near Chennai, approved by the USFDA, which sells to US distributors under partners' labels (B2B, ~70%) and, since 2025, under its own label through Caplin Steriles USA (~30%).

sections.title: History: 35 years, one founder, no acquisitions of note, and one outside investor in the US arm

blocks.p: C.C. Paarthipan founded Caplin in 1990 and listed it in 1994. It went to Angola and then to Latin America in the early 2000s; his son Ashok has run Latin America since 2002. The "stock-and-sale" model (own warehouses, local subsidiaries, outsourcing from China and India) dates from 2005-06. The US business began in 2014 with Caplin Steriles; its plant passed its first USFDA inspection in 2016 and shipped to the US from 2018. In Jan-2019 Eight Roads Ventures (Fidelity International's proprietary investment arm) and F-Prime Capital put ₹218 cr into Caplin Steriles through compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) that convert into **at least 25.29%** of Caplin Steriles. Since then Caplin has funded a ₹600 cr and then a ~₹1,000 cr expansion from its own cash, bought an API plant in Vizag (2022), built an oncology plant (Caplin One Labs), opened subsidiaries in Chile and Mexico, launched its own US label (2025) and bought 15 ANDAs (FY26). There has been no equity issue (other than ESOPs), no buyback and no bonus issue in the last five years, and no large acquisition.

sections.title: Industry: two very different markets: small, credit-driven Latin American generics and the US sterile injectables market

bullets: Caplin sells mostly in small Central American and Caribbean markets (Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Panama, Costa Rica), where multinationals sell brands and local makers are small; >80% of its LatAm revenue is private market (pharmacies), the rest government tenders (ICICI Direct Q3FY26 call notes; Ashok Partheeban: 18-20% institutional in Central America).

Registrations are the entry barrier: 951 products registered in Guatemala, 689 in Nicaragua, 632 in Honduras, 504 in the Dominican Republic, 468 in El Salvador, 354 in Ecuador (AR FY26 registration map). Each new market (Chile, Mexico, Colombia) takes years of filings and bio-studies.
Larger markets are tender-heavy (Mexico, Chile); Mexico gives local manufacturers a price advantage in public tenders (management: 16%; ICICI Direct: 10-15% on margin).

Currencies: El Salvador, Panama and Ecuador use the US dollar; Guatemala and Costa Rica are stable; Nicaragua and Honduras move 3-4% (Chairman, 14-May-2026). The rupee fell from an average ₹88.4/$ in FY26 to ₹94.65/$ at Mar-26 (AR FY26 AOC-1), which lifts rupee revenue.

US sterile injectables: chronic shortages of older injectables keep pricing better than in oral generics; three large wholesalers control ~70% of distribution (Chairman: Caplin targets the remaining ~30% through IDNs and hospital systems).
Capacity and compliance are the constraints: sterile lines take 2-3 years to build and qualify; a USFDA warning letter or import alert can stop supplies from a single-site company.
Generic tariffs: the US administration announced a waiver of tariffs on generics with effect two years out (question on the 12-Aug-2026 call); Caplin manufactures in India.

sections.title: Rest of the World (79% of sales): a pharmacy-level distribution machine in small markets, growing ~3% in dollars; tenders and the rupee do the rest

blocks.p: Caplin's Latin American business is run through its Hong Kong holding company (Caplin Point Far East: FY26 turnover ₹1,274 cr, profit ₹246 cr) and owned importers and distributors in Guatemala (69% owned), Honduras, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Ecuador, Colombia, Chile and Mexico. **How it works:** Caplin registers hundreds of products per country (951 in Guatemala), ships them from India, keeps about six months of fast-moving stock in its own local warehouses (47% of the group's ₹505 cr inventory sits near customers), and sells on credit straight to independent pharmacies and chains; small pharmacies that cannot take its 300-product range are served by two or three co-distributors per country (10-12% of sales); governments buy through tenders (18-20% in Central America; >80% of LatAm revenue is private market). Its shelf share in Central American independent pharmacies is ~41% (Ashok Partheeban), and a planned liquid-oral plant in Guatemala aims to lift that to ~57%. It is now adding **brand marketing** (a CNS range in the Dominican Republic, Guatemala and Nicaragua from Sep-2026) and **new markets**: Chile (own distribution since FY26; 24 running contracts worth $10 mn in FY27 vs $6.2 mn a year earlier; 35 oral solids for the private market), Mexico (29 approvals, 120+ filings planned in 18 months, a plant in Toluca from mid-2027 for the 16% local-maker tender advantage, a distributor acquisition under study) and Colombia (first six products exported).

**The numbers are less exciting than the strategy.** In dollars, LatAm sales were $155 mn in FY26 vs $150 mn (+3%); Central America, the core, grew 7%. Caplin chose margin over volume (gross margin 67% → 71%, PBT 42% → 45%). In rupees the segment grew 9.5% in FY26 and +18% in Q1FY27, helped by a ~$16 mn El Salvador tender (₹50-55 cr shipped in Q4FY26) and a rupee that weakened from ₹85.58/$ at Mar-25 to ₹94.65/$ at Mar-26 (FY26 average ₹88.36; AR FY25 and FY26 AOC-1). **The risks are receivables and currencies:** sales are on credit to pharmacies and governments (Caplin's receivables are 128-138 days); El Salvador, Panama and Ecuador use the dollar, Guatemala and Costa Rica are stable, Nicaragua and Honduras move 3-4% a year (Chairman). Bad debts have been negligible in 20 years, but government receivables (₹46 cr added in Q1FY27) are slower.

sections.title: USA (21% of sales): Caplin Steriles grows 25-30% with 60 ANDAs and its own label, but one plant is full and has just received a 10-observation Form 483

blocks.p: Caplin Steriles (CSL) makes sterile injectables (vials, IV bags, pre-filled syringes, emulsions, suspensions) and ophthalmics at Gummidipoondi, near Chennai. Revenue was ₹453 cr in FY26 (+27.9%) and ₹134 cr in Q1FY27 (+26%); EBITDA ₹142 cr (30%, from 27.9%; 33% in Q4FY26). It has **60 ANDAs approved and 5 under review** (50 developed in-house, 15 bought), 38 launched, a 40+ product pipeline (pre-filled syringes, ophthalmic suspensions, blow-fill-seal) and 110+ filings in other regulated markets (65 approved). Since 2025 it also sells under its **own label** through Caplin Steriles USA: ~₹100 cr in its first full year, ₹43.7 cr in Q1FY27 (vs ₹14.4 cr), weekly orders from the four big wholesalers and contracts with 30+ hospital networks; management targets ~₹200 cr in FY27 and says B2B partners did not shrink. About 85% of CSL revenue is product supply and 15% milestones and profit share.

**Capacity is the constraint.** The plant runs six lines (three older ones mix terminal sterilisation and aseptic filling and break down more often, the Chairman admits) and is "booked out till almost February" 2027. Line 7 starts within 6-7 months of Aug-2026; the COL-II block (five injectable, ophthalmic and BFS lines, room for three more) is due by Mar-2027, but it sits in a different legal entity, so each US product needs a post-approval supplement (batches, three months of stability, ~six months of FDA review): **9-10 months before a moved product sells**. New capacity therefore lifts US revenue mainly from FY28-29. **Compliance is the risk.** The Aug-2024 USFDA inspection ended with zero observations; the unannounced inspection of 13-21 Aug 2026 ended with a **Form 483 listing 10 observations**, which Caplin called procedural, with no data-integrity or repeat observations. Ten observations is a lot for a single-site sterile maker; until the FDA classifies the inspection, approvals and new-line transfers carry more risk than the stock price implies.

sections.title: Plants: oncology is running, APIs and three more plants arrive by FY28; all of it costs before it earns

blocks.p: Caplin is in the middle of its biggest build-out: ~₹1,000-1,100 cr, about half spent by May-2026, all from internal cash. **Already done:** a lyophilised-injectable and dual-chamber-syringe facility at CP1 Puducherry (INVIMA-approved; dual-chamber pre-filled syringes filed in Central America and Ecuador, "no Indian company has brought this technology to Latin America", per Ashok Partheeban); the Vizag general API plant (licensed, 4 APIs validated, 6 scaled up, 12 more by end-2026, first DMFs in FY27); and the **oncology formulation plant** of Caplin One Labs at Kakkalur (capitalised in April 2026 after ministry approval; passed its first regulatory inspection with one minor observation; 6 products in submission batches, 18 more in 12 months for LatAm, US and EU). Caplin One Labs lost ₹16.2 cr in FY26 on ₹33 cr of revenue. **Coming:** the Thervoy oncology API plant (Q4FY27; captive), the Pondicherry oral-solid and dermatology plant (2x today's capacity, Q1FY28; for Mexico, Brazil, the US and EU), the COL-II injectable block at Gummidipoondi (five lines, Q1FY28), Amaris Clinical's expansion to 120 beds (end-FY27; bio-studies at half the cost of outside labs), and the Mexico plant (₹100-125 cr; construction from mid-2027). The target: make 60% of the APIs Caplin uses, and own every dosage form a regulated market wants.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** A real but narrow moat: a distribution and registration franchise in small Latin American markets that throws off cash, but whose growth in dollars has slowed to low single digits; the US business is promising and fast-growing but has no moat yet and a fresh compliance flag. The Latin American franchise earns high returns (45% LatAm PBT margin) because it is too small and too operationally fiddly for multinationals and too far for most Indian rivals; that also caps it. In the US, Caplin is a small single-site supplier among giants; its edge is niche product selection and service, which can disappear with one bad inspection.

sections.title: Revenue 2.5x and EPS 3.0x since FY20, with margins up from 30% to 35%; every year a record

blocks.p: Caplin's revenue grew from ₹863 cr in FY20 to ₹2,187 cr in FY26 (16.8% a year) and EPS from ₹28.4 to ₹84.4 (19.9% a year). EPS has risen every single year, from ₹32.0 in FY21 to ₹84.4 in FY26, with no exceptional charges and no equity raised. Two things drove the margin from 30% to 35%: Latin American gross margins rose (LatAm gross margin 67% → 71% in FY26 alone, per the Vice-Chairman) as Caplin pruned low-margin products, and the US business (Caplin Steriles) went from losses to a 30% EBITDA margin. **Growth is slowing, though:** revenue grew 20-23% a year in FY21-22, 13-16% in FY23-26; FY26 was +12.9% (Latin America +3% in dollars; the rest was the rupee and a large El Salvador tender). Q1FY27 was faster: revenue +19.6%, profit to shareholders +15.8%.

sections.title: Margins: ~60% gross margin, 35% EBITDA margin; the company's 38% 'EBITDA' includes other income

blocks.p: Caplin keeps about 60 paise of every rupee of sales after materials (gross margin 59.8% in Q1FY27, 60.4% in FY26) and spends little on people (9% of sales) because it sells plain generics through distributors and its own small LatAm teams, not through large field forces. Other expenses (freight, registrations, promotion, R&D of ₹79.9 cr) take ~16%. The result is a 35.0% EBITDA margin in FY26 on Screener's basis. **Read the company's numbers with care:** its press release shows an "EBITDA" of ₹876 cr (40.1% of revenue) because it adds other income (₹115.5 cr, mostly interest on the cash pile); before other income it is ₹761 cr. By segment, Rest of the World (Latin America and Africa) earned a 36.4% pre-tax margin in FY26 and the USA 12.4% (Caplin Steriles' EBITDA margin was 30%, 33% in Q4FY26). The US margin is rising fast (24.8% pre-tax in Q1FY27); the Rest of World margin is drifting down (37.5% in Q1FY26 → 33.3% in Q1FY27) as Caplin spends on Chile, Mexico, oncology and brand marketing.

sections.title: Capital allocation: ~₹1,000 cr of plants paid from cash flow, a 9-10% payout, and cash still piling up

blocks.p: Caplin funds everything itself and pays out little. Over FY20-26 it generated ₹2,195 cr of operating cash flow, spent ₹1,020 cr on capex and paid only ₹206 cr of dividends; it has never bought back shares and has no debt. The rest (and the rupee's fall, which lifts the value of its overseas cash and receivables) went into a treasury book that reached ₹1,480 cr at Mar-26. Capex has stepped up: ₹248 cr in FY26, ₹55 cr in Q1FY27, against ₹90-190 cr a year before. The ~₹1,000-1,100 cr programme (half spent by May-2026) adds injectable lines for the US (COL-II, five lines plus three in reserve), a 2x oral-solid and dermatology plant in Pondicherry, an oncology API plant and the oncology formulation plant already running; ₹510 cr was left to spend over 18-24 months from May-2026. Mexico (₹100-125 cr), Chile warehouses and a quality lab come on top. Management also wants acquisitions (a distributor in Mexico or Chile, US ANDAs; 15 ANDAs were bought in FY26) and will pay special dividends only "if we don't find" one (Chairman, 12-Aug-2026).

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean P&L, but cash conversion of ~80%, rising working capital and a CCPS that reported EPS ignores

blocks.p: Caplin's P&L is simple: no exceptional items, no capitalised interest, modest capitalised R&D (₹20.8 cr in FY26). Four things deserve attention. **(1) Cash conversion:** operating cash flow was ₹523 cr in FY26 against ₹650 cr of profit (80%, management's own figure); over FY22-26, CFO was 81% of attributable profit. Receivables rose from 91 to 138 days (Screener) and inventory from 149 to 181 days over FY22-26. **(2) Currency:** a ₹141 cr translation gain went straight to reserves in FY26 (net worth +₹745 cr); 11 of 136 receivable days were translation. FX gains in the P&L were ₹18.6 cr. **(3) Other income:** ₹115.5 cr in FY26 (15% of PBT), of which ₹16.8 cr were realised gains on investments (₹3.9 cr in FY25). **(4) The CCPS:** Caplin Steriles' CCPS (₹216.6 cr from Eight Roads and F-Prime) are shown as Caplin Point's own equity and receive no share of profit in the accounts, yet convert into at least 25.29% of Caplin Steriles. At the minimum stake, ₹13.9 cr of FY26 profit (₹1.8 a share, 2.2% of EPS) economically belongs to the holders; the share grows as the US grows.

sections.title: Valuation: 19x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the stock trades at 26.4x our FY28E EPS, far above its 17.7x history

blocks.p: The only broker note standing on 30-Sep-2026 that discloses a method, ICICI Securities (13-Aug-2026), values Caplin on **P/E**: 26x FY28E EPS. ICICI used EV/EBITDA until Feb-2026 and switched in August. With one broker, "the majority" is that broker; P/E is also the house method for thinly covered pharma names (the WOCKPHARMA / FORCEMOT precedent). We value Caplin on **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**. The model's EPS is EPS to shareholders (minorities in the tax line) and the company reports no exceptional items, so it is the right base. EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks only.

The house rule (PLAYBOOK §4, §7c): Caplin's own one-year-forward P/E (price ÷ next full fiscal year's EPS) from Apr-2021 to 30-Sep-2026, every fifth weekly close (58 points; house forwardMedian), leaving out trough years (none: EPS rose every year; each year's EPS was at least 117% of the prior three-year peak, against the 50% test); multiplied by the pharma sector factor for names outside the nine-peer set (the median move of all nine peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep-2026 close against their five-year medians: +8.2%, PLAYBOOK §7c A21; our reproduction +8.2%); rounded to the nearest half-turn. **The turnaround rule does not apply:** earnings did not break upward (no loss or near-zero years); what changed was the multiple, from ~10-15x in 2021-23 to 20-30x since 2024. That re-rating is precisely what the rule asks us not to assume will persist; the post-Apr-2024 window is shown as a sensitivity. **Exceptional items:** the company reports none; Screener tags ~₹15 cr of FY26 other income (mostly realised investment gains) as exceptional, which changes nothing (19x).

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good, frugal business priced as if the US story were already delivered and the 483 did not exist

blocks.p: A debt-free, founder-run generics company with a distribution franchise in Central America and the Caribbean that earns ~45% pre-tax margins, a US injectables arm growing 25-30% a year, ₹1,480 cr of cash and investments and an unbroken record of rising EPS.

₹2,716 is 31.0x trailing and 26.4x our FY28E EPS. Caplin's own one-year-forward P/E has had a median of 17.7x since Apr-2021 and 21.8x even since the Apr-2024 re-rating; its trailing P/E is 34.2% above its five-year median while pharma peers are 8.2% above theirs. The price implies the US business keeps compounding at 25%+ for years and that Latin America re-accelerates; our numbers have neither, and the CCPS holders' claim on Caplin Steriles (≥25.29%) would take another ₹70 a share off our target.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Caplin Point Laboratories (consolidated, ₹ crore), as of 30-Sep-2026 on Q1FY27 results. Net Profit history is the attributable figure (tools/authoring/CAPLIPOINT.patch.js: Screener 'Profit for EPS'); minorities (mainly the 31% of the Guatemala distributor the group does not own) are carried in the tax line (taxBuild), so the model's profit and EPS are to Caplin Point's shareholders. Caplin reports two segments, Rest of the World (Latin America and Africa, 79% of FY26 revenue) and USA (Caplin Steriles, 21%); the engine runs one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path, the segment build sits in `businessLines` and CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue (CAPLIPOINT.mult.js writes revenueGrowth from it). EBITDA is Screener's operating profit, i.e. before other income (the company's own 'EBITDA' of ₹876 cr in FY26 includes ₹116 cr of other income). Other income = treasury yield on the gross treasury book + government grants and miscellaneous income, no FX gains (built in CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js). Screener files the ₹216.6 cr of Caplin Steriles CCPS held by Eight Roads / F-Prime as borrowings; we leave them there (a claim on Caplin Steriles, not Caplin Point equity). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by segment (businessLines; CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js checks the sum). Rest of the World (Latin America + Africa) +14% in FY27E: Q1FY27 +18% (El Salvador tender spill-over, $7 mn of Central American emergency tenders over two quarters, Chile tenders of $12 mn over 18 months); the Vice-Chairman's AR letter lists ~$24 mn of tender wins in Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua plus Chile's $9.5 mn for FY27 against $18 mn a year earlier; in dollars LatAm grew only 3% in FY26 ($150 mn to $155 mn) and Central America 7%, so roughly 6-7 points of FY27E growth is the rupee (FY26 average ₹88.4/$, Mar-26 close ₹94.65/$; AR FY26 AOC-1). FY28E and FY29E +10%: no further currency gain assumed; Chile and Mexico registrations (29 Mexican approvals, 120+ filings planned) start to contribute, management talks of 18-24 months of 'gestation'. USA (Caplin Steriles, incl. its US front-end) +25% in FY27E: guided 25-30% for FY27 (14-May-2026 call), Q1 +26%, own label targeted at ~₹200 cr vs ~₹100 cr; but the plant is 'booked out till February' and Line 7 starts only in 6-7 months (12-Aug-2026 call), and the 10-observation Form 483 of 21-Aug-2026 adds risk. FY28E and FY29E +20%: new capacity (Line 7, then five lines in the COL-II block from Q1FY28) needs 9-10 months of post-approval supplements per product before it sells into the US, so growth slows from FY26's 28% until FY29.

businessLines._why: Segment revenue, consolidated results and AR FY26 note 26 (disaggregation): USA ₹453.40 cr, Rest of the World ₹1,733.79 cr = revenue from operations ₹2,187.19 cr (sale of products ₹2,083.90 cr, service income ₹87.48 cr, export incentives ₹15.81 cr). The USA segment equals Caplin Steriles' consolidated turnover (₹453.40 cr, AR FY26 AOC-1), so it includes CSL's small non-US regulated-market sales.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener operating margin (before other income): 32.6% FY24, 33.6% FY25, 35.0% FY26, 35.0% in Q1FY27 (ICICI Direct table: 34.8% / 35.0%). Gross margin 59.8% in Q1FY27, guided to stay ~60% (CFO, 12-Aug-2026; the long-standing commitment is 55%). Mix helps: Caplin Steriles' EBITDA margin rose to 30% in FY26 (33% in Q4FY26) from 27.9%, and LatAm's PBT margin rose from 42% to 45% (AR FY26). Costs that hold it back: the oncology plant (Caplin One Labs, PBT −₹19 cr in FY26), the Vizag API unit and Amaris Clinical are not yet breaking even (14-May-2026 call); the Rest of World segment's PBT margin slid from 37.5% in Q1FY26 to ~33% in Q1FY27; Middle East war freight and raw-material inflation. FY27E 35.0% (Q1 level). FY28E 34.8%: the COL-II injectable block and the new Pondicherry OSD/derma plant start (Q1FY28) with staff and overheads ahead of revenue. FY29E 35.2%: utilisation and the US mix. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹28 cr of EBITDA (~3% of FY28E EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex ₹248 cr in FY26 (Screener cash flow; CFO 14-May-2026). Of the ~₹1,000-1,100 cr programme, ₹510 cr remained to be spent over 18-24 months from May-2026 (CFO): COL-II injectable block at Gummidipoondi, the Pondicherry OSD/derma plant, the Thervoy oncology API plant, IV-bag line expansion; Q1FY27 capex ₹55 cr. Not in that figure: the Mexico plant (₹100-125 cr, ICICI Direct Q3FY26 note; construction from mid-2027, AR FY26), Chile warehouses and a quality lab, Amaris expansion to 120 beds. FY27E ₹320 cr, FY28E ₹300 cr (programme tail + Mexico start), FY29E ₹220 cr (Mexico completion + maintenance ~₹100 cr).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹72.8 cr = 8.0% of average gross block (₹859 → ₹965 cr, Screener); Q1FY27 ₹21.6 cr (₹86.5 cr annualised) after the oncology injectable plant and CSL Line 6 were capitalised in April 2026. The engine depreciates capex at once while CWIP (₹234 cr) is held flat, so 8.0%: FY27E ~₹90 cr, FY28E ~₹114 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: FY26 treasury income ₹85.3 cr (interest ₹66.34 cr, realised gains ₹16.81 cr, fair-value gains ₹2.14 cr; AR FY26 note 27) on an average treasury book of ₹1,331 cr (cash, bank deposits and current and non-current investments: ₹1,181.9 cr at Mar-25, ₹1,480.1 cr at Mar-26) = 6.4%. The engine applies the yield to its opening net cash, which deducts the ₹216.6 cr CCPS and ₹4.6 cr of leases and loans that Screener files as borrowings; the yield on that gap is added back in otherIncome (CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js), so in effect 6.4% is earned on the whole gross book. Management is moving 'up the risk chain' into credit and debt funds (12-Aug-2026 call); we assume no change in yield.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built in CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js from AR FY26 note 27: (1) 6.4% on the ₹221 cr gap between the gross treasury book and the engine's net cash (the CCPS and leases are not interest-bearing debt), so the yield applies to the whole ₹1,480 cr book; (2) government grants ₹2.38 cr and miscellaneous income ₹9.25 cr (FY26), held flat. Left out: FX gains (₹18.62 cr in FY26, ₹20.78 cr in FY25), which depend on the rupee's fall against the dollar and the currencies of Caplin's markets; a weaker rupee is already in our FY27E revenue. FY27E total other income ≈ ₹106 cr vs ₹115.5 cr reported in FY26 (₹96.9 cr excluding FX) and ₹126 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 including FX.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹0.87 cr (interest on borrowings ₹0.54 cr, leases ₹0.33 cr; AR FY26 note 31); Q1FY27 ₹0.18 cr. No bank debt (Vice-Chairman, 12-Aug-2026).
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: no minority line). Built in `taxBuild`: tax at 20.5% of PBT (FY26 19.1%, Q1FY27 20.5% 'in line with our target of 20%', CFO 12-Aug-2026; ~21% per the Q3FY26 call) plus minorities. Engine rate = (20.5% x PBT + minorities) / PBT, written from the build by CAPLIPOINT.mult.js. The model's profit and EPS are therefore to Caplin Point's shareholders.

taxBuild._note: Engine tax rate = (tax on PBT + minorities) / PBT. ₹ crore.
taxBuild._why: Minorities: FY24 ₹4 cr, FY25 ₹4.78 cr, FY26 ₹8.49 cr, Q1FY27 ₹2.18 cr (Q1FY26 −₹2.04 cr): mainly the 31% of Nuevos Eticos Neo Ethicals S.A., Guatemala (AR FY26 note 43), plus 0.1% of Argus Salud. Grown in line with the Rest of World business. The Eight Roads / F-Prime CCPS in Caplin Steriles take no share of profit in the accounts (they sit inside equity attributable to owners); their claim is shown separately in the valuation.

assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹8 a share (₹4 interim paid 8-Jun-2026 + ₹4 final approved at the 25-Sep-2026 AGM) = ₹60.8 cr, 9.5% of EPS; FY25 ₹6 (8.5%); FY24 ₹5. Caplin has never bought back shares. Management prefers acquisitions (a Mexican or Chilean distributor, ANDAs) and capex, and offers dividends only if no acquisition comes (Chairman, 12-Aug-2026). We keep 10%, so cash builds; no acquisition is modelled.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity: 6.5% + 1.0 x 6% = 12.5%. Caplin has no debt and ₹1,480 cr of gross treasury, so WACC ≈ cost of equity. Beta 1.0, above Ajanta and Ipca (0.8-0.9): small and politically volatile markets (Central America, Ecuador), currency and receivable risk (128 days), one US sterile site carrying a fresh 10-observation Form 483, and a founder-led board.
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5% nominal in rupees: generic volumes in Latin America and US injectables grow mid-single digit in dollars, plus some rupee depreciation.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~12% (FY29E) to 7% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 33%: below the 35% of FY26-27 because the US mix (30% EBITDA margin) rises and LatAm generic pricing is competitive; above the 30-31% of FY21-23.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: 5% of revenue (FY24-26 average ~10% during the ₹1,000 cr programme; FY21-22 ~3-7%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Latin America keeps growing in the mid-teens as Chile and Mexico tenders and private-market launches scale and the rupee stays weak; the Form 483 closes without escalation, Line 7 and COL-II start on time and the US grows 25-30% a year; the oncology plant and API unit break even.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The 483 escalates (warning letter or import alert) and the US stalls; Central American tenders lapse after FY27 and dollar growth reverts to the 3% of FY26; receivables stretch further in government markets and new plants run below break-even for longer.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Caplin: the only broker note standing on 30-Sep-2026 that discloses a method (ICICI Securities, 13-Aug-2026) uses P/E, 26x FY28E EPS; ICICI used EV/EBITDA until Feb-2026. P/E is also the house method for thinly covered pharma names. 19x Sep-28E EPS = Caplin's 17.7x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (house forwardMedian, 58 points, reported EPS: the company reports no exceptional items; no trough years, EPS rose every year from ₹32.0 in FY21 to ₹84.4 in FY26) x the pharma sector factor of 1.082 (median of the nine-peer set's trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +8.2% for names outside the set, PLAYBOOK §7c A21; reproduced at 8.19%) = 19.2x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. Bull 23x / bear 13.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (21.2x / 12.6x) x the factor. No growth, returns or own-move adjustment; the post-re-rating window since Apr-2024 (21.8x, 24x with the same-window peer move) is a sensitivity row. The model's EPS is EPS to shareholders (minorities in the tax line). Checked in CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js; written by CAPLIPOINT.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check. Caplin's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 15.5x (Screener); times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor (+7.5%, PLAYBOOK §7c A21) = 16.7x, rounded to 16.5x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) plus the engine's net cash at Sep-2027 (which deducts the ₹216.6 cr Caplin Steriles CCPS at book). Bull 20.5x / bear 13x = 75th / 25th percentile x the factor.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Caplin: the only broker note standing on 30-Sep-2026 that discloses a method (ICICI Securities, 13-Aug-2026) uses P/E, 26x FY28E EPS; ICICI used EV/EBITDA until Feb-2026. P/E is also the house method for thinly covered pharma names. 19x Sep-28E EPS = Caplin's 17.7x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (house forwardMedian, 58 points, reported EPS: the company reports no exceptional items; no trough years, EPS rose every year from ₹32.0 in FY21 to ₹84.4 in FY26) x the pharma sector factor of 1.082 (median of the nine-peer set's trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +8.2% for names outside the set, PLAYBOOK §7c A21; reproduced at 8.19%) = 19.2x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. Bull 23x / bear 13.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (21.2x / 12.6x) x the factor. No growth, returns or own-move adjustment; the post-re-rating window since Apr-2024 (21.8x, 24x with the same-window peer move) is a sensitivity row. The model's EPS is EPS to shareholders (minorities in the tax line). Checked in CAPLIPOINT.ctx.js; written by CAPLIPOINT.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check. Caplin's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 15.5x (Screener); times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor (+7.5%, PLAYBOOK §7c A21) = 16.7x, rounded to 16.5x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) plus the engine's net cash at Sep-2027 (which deducts the ₹216.6 cr Caplin Steriles CCPS at book). Bull 20.5x / bear 13x = 75th / 25th percentile x the factor.
